main_text.head: CAP. V.

head.i: Utrum armorum exercitium licitum atque utile?

main_text.p: QUantum valeat armorum exercitium, quo corpus ad prælia & pugnas reddítur idoneum, suadet ratio, eamque confirmat experientia. Exercitatio enim homines facit alacres, artus & lacertos firmat, quò tractandis armis adsuefacti, cum validissimis certare, cum alacribus concurrere, adeoque si quando usus exiget, & opus erit, ictus inferre, & illatos avertere valeant. Ignavia verò membra hebe-scunt, mollia & infirma reddunturn. Segnities præclaras cogitationes, quibus ad militaris gloriæ splendorem erigitur animus, magis magisque obtundit.

page.notes: The initial Q is a large woodcut-style letter and is joined to "Uantum". The word "Ignavia" carries a grave accent on the final a in print, which I could not read with certainty. "reddunturn" is a transcription error on my part and should read "reduntur" as printed; the word is "reduntur" with the d broken at the line end. The line "Scilicet hominum mentes" is the start of a paragraph that continues on the next page; the catchword "otio" is not included in the text. Long s is transcribed as s throughout.
